resources.string: Linear calibration with a gauge block
Type the true size of the gauge block. If you touch the two outer faces with an edge finder, add the diameter of the stylus.
Move the axis to the %1$s edge of the block. Then push Continue.
Turn the axis to the 0° position. Then push Continue.
Turn the axis clockwise exactly 5 full revolutions. Then push Continue.
Do not move the axis. The app reads the input for up to 15 seconds.
Resolution: %1$s counts per inch (%2$s µm for each count)
Resolution: %1$s counts per revolution (%2$s° for each count)
Direction: normal. The count goes up from the first position to the second position.
Direction: reversed. The count goes down from the first position to the second position. Apply sets the reverse direction.
Apply writes the resolution, the direction, and the status Calibrated to the encoder settings of %1$s. Discard writes nothing.
The calibration was not saved. The adapter profile is not in the store.
Type a block size that is more than 0.
A longer block gives a more accurate result. Use a block %1$s long. Push Continue to use this block.
The app got no reading from %1$s. Make sure that the input is connected and that its mode sends counts.
The app got %1$d readings from %2$s. It needs %3$d or more. Push Retry to read the input again.
The readings changed by %1$s counts while the axis did not move. Hold the axis still and push Retry.
The two positions are less than %1$d counts apart. Move the axis to the second position, then push Retry.
The link to the adapter stopped during the reading. Wait for the link, then push Retry.
This machine profile has no adapter profile. Connect the adapter and make its adapter profile first.
The tachometer input has no calibration. Set its pulses for each revolution in the adapter details.
The kind of this input is Disabled. Select Linear or Angular in the encoder settings first.
